title: Reading Simple Words
introduction: Learn about reading simple words through simple examples and practice.
definition: Join the sounds in short words to read them. For example, c-a-t makes cat.
rules: Blend the sounds from left to right to read a word.
Try short words with different vowels: cat, bed, pig, fox and cup.
Some words have two consonants together, such as flag and frog. Learn these gradually.
Say each sound slowly, then blend them together.

vocabulary.description: A container used to carry things.
Material made of connected threads with spaces between them.
An animal with a bushy tail.
A container for cooking or growing plants.
A vehicle that carries many passengers.
A piece of material covering part of a floor.

examples.question: Blend b-a-g.
steps: Say the sounds, then join them without pauses.

examples.question: Blend n-e-t.
steps: Say /n/, the short e sound and /t/.

examples.question: Blend p-i-g.
steps: Join the three sounds to read pig.

examples.question: Blend c-u-p.
steps: Join the sounds to read cup.

exercises.solution: Blend /m/, the short a sound and /p/ into one word.
